description:
Found during the bedrock-61c.2 audit; pre-existing.

`Health.compute_health_from_worker_info/1` (lib/bedrock/service/foreman/health.ex:9-18) folds worker healths with these clauses:

    {:ok, _}, :ok -> :ok
    {:ok, _}, _   -> :starting        # <-- downgrades a recorded failure
    {:failed_to_start, _}, :ok -> :starting
    {:failed_to_start, _}, _   -> {:failed_to_start, :at_least_one_failed_to_start}

The second clause overwrites an accumulated `{:failed_to_start, _}` back to `:starting`, so the verdict depends on element order. Measured:

    [ok, bad, bad] -> {:failed_to_start, :at_least_one_failed_to_start}
    [bad, bad, ok] -> :starting
    [bad, ok, bad] -> {:failed_to_start, :at_least_one_failed_to_start}
    [ok, bad]      -> :starting

`recompute_health/1` folds `Map.values(t.workers)`, and for <32 keys Erlang flatmaps iterate in term order — so the verdict depends on how worker ids sort. A single failed worker whose id sorts before a healthy one yields `:starting`, hiding the failure; the same set in the other order reports it.

## Failure scenario

A node with worker ids "aaaa" (failed) and "zzzz" (healthy) reports `:starting` forever — indistinguishable from still-booting — while ids "zzzz" (failed) and "aaaa" (healthy) correctly report `{:failed_to_start, _}`. Operators cannot tell a wedged worker from a slow one, and the signal flips if a worker id changes.

## Fix

A failure should be absorbing: once any worker has failed, no later healthy worker should clear it. Likely `Enum.reduce` over explicit counts (any failed -> failed; else any not-ok -> starting; else ok) rather than a pairwise fold whose result depends on order.

## Test (write first, must fail)

Property or table test asserting the verdict is invariant under `Enum.shuffle/1` of the same worker-info list, across all combinations of ok/failed/stopped.
title: [BUG] Foreman health fold is order-dependent: a healthy worker downgrades a recorded failure
